title: George Washington Carver at Tuskegee
summary: Wilson recalls Carver as a quiet chemist with a fresh white flower in his lapel, loved but secluded on campus.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was George Washington Carver there at Tuskegee at that time?
Oh yes, I remember him very well. Yeah.
What kind of a man was he, Teddy?
He was a very quiet, pleasant man.
He was in his laboratory in the agricultural building, and always doing his experiments and his work in advanced chemistry.
Yeah, with those little tin cans and that.

Yes, sir -- all of his own equipment. He did marvelous things with natural science and chemistry, and I always remember he always made chapel exercises on Sunday, and he would always wear this white flower in his lapel; always a fresh white flower in his lapel.

And the story around the campus -- everybody loved him, but to the people there, you know, they didn't understand him, really, this advanced chemistry, so he was sort of secluded, yes. He was very different than the average faculty member, the people, the community in those days -- advanced scientist as he was, he couldn't talk that stuff with those people.
But they all loved him, and everybody was very proud of him and because we all knew, and the whole school knew that these giant corporations in the north had
always tried to get him to join their staffs, and do research and chemistry -- everyone knew how highly he was regarded by the federal government, and the intelligentsia of the northern universities.
